tb21_profile.skill: Port a Bayesian model across bindings of the same inference engine: read R/RStan source you are forbidden to run, recover the Stan program and the sampler hyperparameters, express them through a different API with identical semantics and a fixed seed, then run MCMC and report posterior means that match a reference
tb21_profile.domain: Bayesian statistics and MCMC (Stan/NUTS, Gaussian-process regression with alpha/rho/sigma, PyStan 3.10 pinned install and its C++ build), plus R-to-Python scientific translation
tb21_profile.task_form: port-a-script / implement-from-spec, verified numerically: install a pinned library, translate, run the sampler, write plain numeric CSVs that are compared against reference posterior means

verifier_notes: The packet and work/verifier_strength.json disagree sharply for the CalibForge data-science_*_007 family: the packet shows weak/ok for data-science_20260604_002443_007, _20260610_111012_007 and _20260613_152233_007, while verifier_strength.json grades all of them strong. I checked the direction of the disagreement on this family and the newer grading is the defensible one - these tasks are scored on numeric output files compared against reference values, not on file existence - so I used verifier_strength.json and required non-FREE under both sources for final_top10. data-science_20260617_051646_007 is FREE in both and excluded. Separately: CalibForge contains auto-generated filler tasks named '<category>_<timestamp>_inspector.py' that are tagged to a TB2.1 domain but are generic directory-hashing utilities - data-science_20260615_143956_007 is one for this task and scores well lexically; I excluded it and the merge step should filter that whole family.

notes: This is the clearest win for CalibForge of my five, and it is close to a categorical one. The v1 pool has literally zero Stan content: `search <corpus> "PyStan|Stan model|cmdstan|rstan|brms|JAGS"` returns no genuine hit in TMax, TerminalWorld, Recursive-Task-Synthesis or SWE-Smith (every apparent match is the substring 'stan' inside 'understand' or 'instance'). CalibForge supplies a cluster of six R-or-Stan-to-Python porting tasks, three of which reproduce the TB2.1 setup almost line for line - same /app/train_X.csv, /app/train_y.csv, /app/test_X.csv file names, the same 'you may read the R script but may not install or run R' constraint, and the same numeric-CSV deliverable - and all six are strong-verified in work/verifier_strength.json. It also supplies the only Gaussian-process-from-scratch task in the pool, which matters because the TB2.1 model is a GP. SWE-Rebench is the one v1 corpus that contributes something real: it has PyMC, NumPyro, GPflow and GPyTorch repositories, and pymc-devs__pymc-7637 is specifically about seeded sampling determinism, which the TB2.1 task pins with random_seed=1. TMax keeps two slots on generic MCMC-posterior work. Terminal-Lego-15k is also near-empty for this task: a grep of all 15,048 instructions for MCMC/Bayesian/posterior/likelihood/Gaussian-process returns four hits, none of them Bayesian, so its list is filled with sample-statistics and regression-fitting exercises scoring 2-3. Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld cannot field 10 defensible candidates at all here - their best entries are generic 'compute numbers and write a CSV' chores scoring 1-2, and their shortlists were driven entirely by the boilerplate overlap on '/app/*.csv' and 'write a Python script'. Two things for the merge step: (1) CalibForge's auto-generated '<category>_<timestamp>_inspector.py' filler tasks name the TB2.1 domain in their text but are generic directory-hashing utilities (data-science_20260615_143956_007 here, software-engineering_20260612_191200_021 under regex-chess) and should be filtered globally; (2) the packet `verifier` field is stale relative to work/verifier_strength.json for much of this CalibForge family - the packet undercounts them as weak/ok where the newer pass says strong.
